bio: Giuseppe Di Guglielmo is a Principal Engineer at Fermilab. He is also an Adjunct Associate Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Northwestern University and a Designated Academic Colleague in the Department of Computer Science at Columbia University. His field is system-level design and hardware acceleration for AI/ML.

He works with scientists to build intelligent detectors for harsh environments, where data has to be processed with ultra-low latency. Recent projects include radiation-resistant chips with embedded ML for the Large Hadron Collider, and ML algorithms for quantum readout and control running in hardware at cryogenic temperatures.

At Fermilab he is part of the AI Program and of the team contributing to the DOE Genesis Mission, where he works on AI-accelerated co-design workflows for scientific microelectronics and instrumentation.

He has over 15 years of experience with high-level synthesis for ASIC and FPGA design and holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science. He contributes to open-source projects for AI/ML acceleration and SoC design, and is an IEEE Senior Member.
